strategyPoints: Tire wear is always a concern here on this abrasive surface. Managing the tires through the long corners will be key.
The pit window opens around lap 15, but teams will be closely monitoring the degradation before making the call.
With a relatively short lap, traffic can become a major factor in the race. Timing the pit stops is crucial.
Fuel consumption will be a factor today. Teams will need to balance performance with fuel efficiency.
The length of the pit lane here at Buenos Aires means a longer pit stop time than some other circuits, so an undercut is less effective.
The Historic layout's blend of high-speed corners and tight sections presents a unique challenge for setting up the car.
A safety car period could really shake things up. Teams will need to be ready to react quickly to any unexpected events.
With only one DRS zone, overtaking could be tricky. Getting a good run out of the final corner will be essential.
weatherCommentary: The wind could be a factor today, especially on the back straight. It could affect the car's stability under braking.
The temperature is rising here at the Autódromo. Expect to see tire management become even more critical as the race progresses.
The humidity is quite high today, which will be tough on the drivers in the cockpit.
There's a chance of rain later in the afternoon. That could throw a real curveball into the strategy.
The bright sunshine is reflecting off the track, making it difficult for the drivers to judge the braking points.
